analyst_view.overall: Early view: Union have tightened up under Mauro Lustrinelli after conceding 17 goals in their first four games, but they were toothless at Freiburg (no shots in the first half) and still lack a reliable striker. Leipzig have won all five home games under Martín Demichelis yet have taken only three of their 18 points away from home, and they have Champions League football the following week.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Union were unbeaten in four league games before Freiburg while conceding only twice, playing from a deeper block, and Leipzig have been far less convincing away than at home. Union's own attack, seven goals in nine, is the main reason to expect a modest total.

corners.text: The site expects 9.2 corners. Leipzig should have most of the ball, which usually produces corners against a low block, but Union offered almost nothing going forward at Freiburg, so their own share may be small. These two effects roughly cancel, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. I lean a little higher: Julian Schuster called games against Union 'always very physical', and seven yellow cards were shown when Köln visited the Alte Försterei recently. A Union side near the bottom, at home against a Leipzig team that counters quickly, is likely to commit tactical fouls.

shots.text: The site has 25.1 shots, 11.4 for Union. That home figure looks high for a side that had no shots at all in the first half at Freiburg and has struggled to find a striker, with Andrej Ilic, Oliver Burke and Emmanuel Latte Lath all short of form or fitness earlier this autumn. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 on target. With Union's attack blunt and their plan built on keeping the score low, I expect fewer, and Leipzig away have not been as sharp as their 23-2 home goal record suggests. I lean slightly lower.
